chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abu Himmam Isma'il ibn Himmam, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ghazwan, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said:

Whoever obeys his wife in four matters, God will throw him into the Fire face down (on his nose). It was asked: What are they? He said: Wearing thin/transparent clothes, going to public baths, attending wedding parties, and attending mourning ceremonies.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things a man should not obey his wife in according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq identifies four specific domains—thin clothing, public baths, wedding feasts, and mourning ceremonies—where a man's obedience to his wife leads to being cast into Hellfire face-down. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ittiba'* (following) in matters of modesty and social conduct, warning that yielding to a wife's preferences in these areas may compromise religious principles or lead to excess. The imagery of being cast 'on his nostrils' signifies a humiliating and complete submission to worldly desires rather than divine command.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-3 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Abi Himmam - Isma’il ibn Himmam, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sa’id ibn Qazvan, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB) , on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB), “God will throw whoever obeys his wife regarding four issues into the Fire..” He (MGB) was asked, “What are they?” The Imam (MGB) replied, “Regarding wearing transparent clothes, going to public baths, attending wedding parties and going to mourning ceremonies.
